article_content: 'Ten-year-old knife-thrower Edward Pinder practices an unusual skill each night: hurling eight-inch blades at his mother, Erika, after finishing his homework.' 'The routine takes place in a custom-built circus ring at their home in Bisbrooke, Leicestershire, where Edward has never missed or harmed 37-year-old Erika.' 'Performing since he was a toddler, Edward now appears with the family’s traveling show, Pinder’s Circus, which traces its roots back to 1850.' 'During shows, Edward remains calm while his mother admits she feels a small rush of nerves when she steps in front of his knives.' 'He hopes to push his act further, planning to throw stars and axes, and may even involve his father, Eddy, a 38-year-old clown.' 'Erika says the act works because she and her son trust one another, and so far, everything has gone smoothly.' 'Even though Erika can get anxious, she praises Edward’s calm focus, adding that the audience is always enthralled.' 'Eddy proudly states that Edward is likely the youngest knife-thrower in Britain and possibly in all of Europe.'

'Oppvisningen foregår i en spesialbygd sirkusring hjemme i Bisbrooke, Leicestershire, der Edward aldri har bommet eller skadet 37 år gamle Erika.' 'Siden han var smårolling har Edward opptrådt i familiens omreisende show, Pinder’s Circus, som kan spores tilbake til 1850.' 'Under forestillingene er Edward rolig, mens moren innrømmer at hun får et snev av nerver idet hun stiller seg foran knivene hans.' 'Han håper å utvikle nummeret enda mer, blant annet ved å kaste stjerner og økser, og kan til og med involvere faren sin, Eddy, som er 38 år og jobber som klovn.' 'Erika sier at nummeret fungerer fordi hun og sønnen stoler på hverandre, og så langt har alt gått knirkefritt.' 'Selv om Erika kan bli nervøs, roser hun Edwards rolige konsentrasjon, og forteller at publikum alltid er begeistret.' 'Eddy sier stolt at Edward sannsynligvis er den yngste knivkasteren i Storbritannia, og muligens i hele Europa.'

article_content: Baroness Hale of Richmond, the only female Supreme Court justice, has criticized the British legal profession for failing to promote women to senior positions, attributing it to longstanding 'unconscious sexism.' Speaking at the London School of Economics, she highlighted how many talented female candidates are overlooked because employers are not used to working with women. She stated: 'There are many unconscious assumptions and judgments made when people do not realize they are doing so. The more accustomed people become to having women and ethnic minority colleagues around, the less this is a problem, because they understand how we behave. However, if you hardly ever see a woman, it is difficult to properly assess a female candidate.' Lady Hale argued that the legal profession remains weighted in favor of well-known lawyers and would benefit from greater diversity. Referring to the current situation as 'terrible,' she also expressed frustration that gender equality in higher judicial ranks has lagged behind other countries. Appointed a High Court judge in 1994, she said she supports a tie-breaker system in which, if multiple candidates are equally qualified, a minority candidate should be chosen. She described the approach as 'affirmative action' rather than 'positive discrimination.' Law Society figures reveal that 47% of solicitors and 35% of barristers are female, and more than half of new entrants to the profession since 1993 have been women. Yet, there are only 21 female judges out of 148 in the Court of Appeal and High Court. According to research by Laurence Simons, a legal recruitment firm, the average female lawyer still earns around £51,396 less per year than her male counterpart.

Under en tale ved London School of Economics påpekte hun hvordan mange dyktige kvinnelige kandidater ikke blir vurdert fordi arbeidsgivere ikke er vant til å jobbe med kvinner. Hun uttalte: 'Det finnes mange ubevisste antagelser og vurderinger som gjøres uten at folk innser det. Jo mer folk venner seg til å ha kvinner og etniske minoriteter i miljøet, desto mindre blir dette et problem, fordi de vet hvordan vi oppfører oss. Men hvis du nesten aldri ser en kvinne, er det vanskelig å vurdere en kvinnelig kandidat på riktig måte.' Lady Hale argumenterte for at jussektoren fortsatt favoriserer kjente advokater og vil ha nytte av større mangfold. Hun beskrev situasjonen som 'forferdelig' og uttrykte frustrasjon over at likestilling i høyere rettsinstanser henger etter andre land. Da hun ble utnevnt til High Court-dommer i 1994, uttalte hun at hun støtter et system der, hvis flere kandidater har lik kompetanse, bør en kandidat fra en minoritetsgruppe velges. Hun beskrev dette som 'affirmative action' i stedet for 'positiv diskriminering.' Tall fra Law Society viser at 47% av advokater og 35% av barristers er kvinner, og siden 1993 har over halvparten av nyutdannede i bransjen vært kvinner. Likevel er det bare 21 kvinnelige dommere av 148 i Court of Appeal og High Court. Ifølge forskning fra Laurence Simons, et rekrutteringsfirma for juridiske stillinger, tjener kvinnelige advokater fremdeles rundt 51 396 pund mindre i året enn sine mannlige kolleger.

article_content: A gifted 13-year-old footballer, Quinton Barham, is in critical condition after suffering a cardiac arrest in the middle of an under-14s cup match in Bromham, Wiltshire. He complained of chest pain shortly after scoring his third goal, then collapsed moments later. Quick-thinking first aiders and an off-duty paramedic started CPR on Quinton before an air ambulance arrived to help restart his heart. He was then rushed to Bristol Children's Hospital, where he remains on life support. According to his father, Paul, doctors believe Quinton's pulmonary artery runs between his two heart chambers instead of passing through one of them, and the strain of intense exercise may have caused the artery to collapse. Paul described the terrifying moment when his son's eyes rolled back and he became unresponsive. He credits the immediate CPR provided by bystanders for saving Quinton's life. Although Quinton has shown minor signs of improvement, such as flexing his fingers, doctors are still concerned about potential brain damage. Quinton, the youngest of four children, lives for football. His cousin, Carly, describes him as a die-hard Manchester United fan who devotes every spare moment to the sport. She says he would be devastated if doctors advise him not to play again. Fabrice Muamba, a professional footballer who collapsed from cardiac arrest in a high-profile match, retweeted Carly's message of support for Quinton. The Barham family remains hopeful that Quinton will recover and eventually return to the pitch.

article_content: Southampton have reverted to their traditional style after unveiling their new home kit for the 2014/15 season. Saints released the strip on Friday, featuring the club's familiar red and white stripes. Familiar sight: The new home kit showcases Southampton's iconic stripes. In an advertisement, Jose Fonte (center) appears alongside Jay Rodriguez (left) and James Ward-Prowse (right). Accompanied by the slogan 'the stripes are back,' the trio model the south coast outfit's latest kit, celebrating the club's long and rich heritage. The red and white striped jersey boasts a red v-neck collar and sleeves, paired with black shorts. Supporters can expect to see Ronald Koeman's side donning red socks with black hoops, a stark contrast to the club's previous kits from the past two seasons, which featured an all-red ensemble. Many fans were upset by the stripe-less look, with one supporter stating in a forum: 'Red and white stripes are what Saints are associated with. It just won't look right.' Another added: 'I see nothing to like about the home kit when it doesn't reflect our traditional colors.' The St. Mary's outfit has confirmed that the away kit will be revealed in the near future, promising further excitement for fans. A teaser video shows Koeman taking the helm at Saints as he embarks on his new role.

article_content: By James Rush. Published: 13:47 EST, 11 April 2013. Updated: 06:44 EST, 12 April 2013. Gymnastics coach Bob Bellew walked free from court today after he admitted a series of sexual abuse charges over 40 years. Bellew, 66, is an internationally renowned gymnastics coach who abused seven girls as young as six. He has published books on gymnastics, taught at schools across the UK, and previously served on committees planning the 2012 Olympics. He was chief coach of the Tower Hamlets Schools gym and dance display team and once received the ‘Order of the Smile’, a UN-recognized citation for adults who provide exceptional care for children. He admitted a string of sexual abuse charges spanning four decades, involving seven girls he instructed. However, he was spared jail at Snaresbrook Crown Court by Judge Joanna Korner, who noted his ‘genuine remorse.’ Victims expressed outrage, issuing a statement criticizing the British justice system for not imposing a harsher punishment. During the hearing, Bellew, who appeared visibly shaken, admitted touching three children at a south London primary school in the 1970s. He helped them with alleged ‘groin injuries,’ removing their clothing and groping them. He also molested the daughter of a friend under the guise of tutoring and stroked another girl’s thigh at his home. He committed further offenses between 1998 and 2004, touching two teenagers on the pretext of assisting them with routines. Judge Korner imposed a 15-month prison sentence, suspended for two years, and barred Bellew from working with children. She noted that these were isolated offenses and believed that his effective punishment began with the loss of his professional standing. Bellew pleaded guilty to eight of 17 charges, including seven counts of indecent assault and one of sexual touching, just weeks before his trial. Nine additional charges remain on the court file. In a statement, some victims said, ‘This sentence shows everything wrong with the British justice system. He has had this hanging over him for only a few years, while we have lived with it our entire lives.’ After the offenses came to light, some victims who excelled in sports said Bellew’s abuse destroyed what should have been a safe and trusting environment, leaving lasting emotional damage. Prosecutor Rekha Kodikara explained that the incidents spanned two distinct periods: the 1970s and the 1990s to early 2000s, facilitated by his position of trust as a coach. Although he initially denied charges, Bellew admitted guilt in court. In a probation report, he backtracked, insisting the touching was not sexual and shifting blame onto the victims. His lawyer, Barry Kogan, said Bellew was ashamed and in denial, but insisted his remorse was genuine. Detective Constable Lewi Fenton expressed disappointment with the sentence and urged any other victims to contact the authorities.

Han innrømmet en rekke seksuelle overgrep mot sju jenter over fire tiår, men unngikk fengsel i Snaresbrook Crown Court da dommer Joanna Korner viste til hans «ekte anger». Ofrene uttrykte raseri i en uttalelse og kritiserte det britiske rettssystemet for å ikke gi en strengere straff. Under høringen innrømmet en tydelig rystet Bellew å ha berørt tre barn på en barneskole i Sør-London på 1970-tallet. Han hjalp dem angivelig med «lyskeskader» ved å fjerne klærne deres og beføle dem. Mellom 1998 og 2004 begikk han ytterligere overgrep mot to tenåringer under påskudd av å hjelpe dem med rutiner. Dommer Korner ga ham en fengselsstraff på 15 måneder, betinget i to år, og forbød Bellew å arbeide med barn. Hun påpekte at dette var enkeltstående hendelser, og at tapet av hans profesjonelle anseelse allerede fungerte som en straff. Bellew erkjente seg skyldig i åtte av 17 tiltalepunkter, inkludert sju tilfeller av usømmelig overgrep og ett tilfelle av seksuell berøring, bare uker før rettssaken. Ni ytterligere tiltalepunkter ligger i rettsarkivet. I en felles uttalelse sa noen av ofrene: «Denne dommen viser alt som er galt med det britiske rettssystemet. Han har bare hatt dette hengende over seg i noen få år, mens vi har levd med det hele livet.» Etter at overgrepene ble kjent, fortalte noen av ofrene som utmerket seg i idrett, at Bellews overgrep ødela det som skulle vært et trygt og tillitsfullt miljø, og etterlot varige følelsesmessige sår. Aktor Rekha Kodikara forklarte at hendelsene fant sted i to perioder: 1970-årene og mellom 1990 og tidlig på 2000-tallet, og at Bellews tillitsposisjon som trener muliggjorde overgrepene. Selv om han opprinnelig nektet for anklagene, erkjente Bellew skyld i retten. I en tilsynsrapport trakk han seg delvis fra tilståelsen, hevdet at berøringen ikke var seksuell, og la skylden på ofrene. Hans advokat, Barry Kogan, sa at Bellew følte skam og fornektelse, men insisterte på at angeren var ekte. Etterforsker Lewi Fenton uttrykte skuffelse over straffen og oppfordret alle andre ofre til å kontakte myndighetene.

article_content: Published by Richard Marsden on 15 December 2013 and updated the next day, this article details how small shop owners and the fast-food chain Subway will soon introduce a five pence fee for each plastic bag given to customers. The Association of Convenience Stores, which speaks for over 33,500 small shops and takeaways, plans to adopt these charges that become mandatory for larger English stores from October 2015. This action follows the Daily Mail’s 'Banish the Bags' campaign, spotlighting the environmental harm caused by plastic bags. In just two years, the use of disposable bags rose to seven billion annually. These bags are often used briefly yet can take centuries to decompose. They pollute landscapes and pose serious risks to marine life and birds that ingest them or become trapped. Revenue from the new charge, starting in 2015, will support charities dealing with wildlife and environmental impacts. Shane Brennan, from the Association of Convenience Stores, mentioned a 'strong appetite' among retailers to apply the charges but emphasizes a need for exemption from regulations imposed on larger retailers—those retailers must report profits back to the government. Meanwhile, Subway, with 1,600 locations across Britain, will encourage its franchises to charge for bags. Keep Britain Tidy suggests extending charges to all small shops to avoid confusion where franchises of the same brand have varying fee policies. Under Environment Secretary Owen Paterson’s plan, England’s supermarkets and department stores will start charging for single-use plastic bags in 2015. Scotland will introduce a similar fee next year. Wales made bag fees compulsory in 2011 and saw an 80% drop in usage, while Northern Ireland began at five pence in April and is set to increase to ten pence.
translated_content: Publisert av Richard Marsden 15. desember 2013 og oppdatert dagen etter, beskriver denne artikkelen hvordan småbutikkeiere og hurtigmatkjeden Subway snart vil innføre et gebyr på fem pence for hver plastpose som gis til kundene. Association of Convenience Stores, som representerer over 33 500 små butikker og takeaway-steder, har planer om å vedta disse avgiftene som blir obligatoriske for større butikker i England fra oktober 2015. Dette følger Daily Mails 'Banish the Bags'-kampanje, som fremhever miljøskader forårsaket av plastposer. I løpet av bare to år har bruken av engangsposer økt til syv milliarder årlig. Disse posene brukes ofte kort tid, men kan ta århundrer å brytes ned. De forurenser landskapet og utgjør en alvorlig fare for marint dyreliv og fugler som spiser dem eller vikler seg inn i dem. Inntekter fra det nye gebyret, som starter i 2015, skal gå til veldedige organisasjoner som arbeider med dyr og miljø. Shane Brennan, fra Association of Convenience Stores, nevnte en 'sterk appetitt' blant forhandlere for å ta i bruk avgiftene, men understreker behovet for fritak fra regelverket pålagt større forhandlere – disse forhandlerne må rapportere overskudd til myndighetene. Samtidig vil Subway, med 1 600 lokasjoner i Storbritannia, oppfordre sine franchisetakere til å innføre avgift for poser. Keep Britain Tidy foreslår å utvide avgifter til alle små butikker for å unngå forvirring der franchiser under samme merke kan ha ulike gebyrregler. Under Miljøminister Owen Patersons plan skal supermarkeder og varehus i England begynne å ta betalt for engangsplastposer i 2015. Skottland innfører en lignende avgift neste år. Wales gjorde poseavgift obligatorisk i 2011 og så en nedgang på 80 % i bruk, mens Nord-Irland begynte med fem pence i april og skal øke til ti pence.
